audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Sett levels 1, 2, 3 and 6 and Skill for both item stages, but the prose under it already says level 1 is even, level 6 is even, first item 'flips it' to Zaahen and two items are Zaahen's. Zaahen wins 52.31% over 2013 games.
audit.why: The whys[] text and the packet chart agree with each other; only the enum rows are out of step. Packet and mirror both read Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen.
audit.corrected: Row 0 and row 4 to Skill, rows 5 and 6 to Zaahen, in both layers, with ratings 5/10, 5/10, 6/10, 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet defect is 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' and it is accurate — not one number on the page.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1, Facebreaker 16s, The Show Stopper 120s. Zaahen's Q and E are both 10s at rank 1, W 14s, R 110s. Sett's bully window is real but each of his tools has a long gap behind it.
audit.corrected: Put 18s on Haymaker and 16s on Facebreaker so 'step in when he spends it' becomes a countable window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three real errors. (1) The page repeatedly warns about 'his E stun' — Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are on both sides of him; solo in lane it slows. (2) Nothing states that The Show Stopper grounds, which shuts off Zaahen's Aureate Rush dash. (3) Zaahen's E is called 'Golden Onslaught'; the real name is Aureate Rush.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' And Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the missing-interaction rule 'resistances-invalidated' applies — stacking armour is the wrong answer and was never said.
audit.corrected: Say Facebreaker slows in a 1v1, that his R is the real lock and it grounds your dash, and that Haymaker's centre true damage ignores the armour you bought.

edits.before: Shield + true damage. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1, true damage in the centre — bait it first.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Haymaker's centre is true damage — armour will not save you; sidestep.

edits.before: Coin-flipping into an unknown matchup — respect what you have not seen until you have seen it twice.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides — solo in lane it slows, so his R is the real lock.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — 18s at rank 1, shield plus true damage. Bait it. - Facebreaker 16s: solo in lane it only slows. - The Show Stopper grounds you: hold Aureate Rush until it is spent.

edits.before: By 6 your Final Retribution (R) plus your Q Darkin Glaive and E Golden Onslaught let you match his all-in; his The Show Stopper (R) is a strong displacement lock but you have the tools to trade back, and the lane starts leveling toward you.
edits.after: By 6 Grim Deliverance (R, 110s) plus The Darkin Glaive (Q, 10s) and Aureate Rush (E, 10s) let you match his all-in — but The Show Stopper grounds you, so hold the dash until he has spent it, then pull him back and heal off the damage.

edits.before: Sett takes levels 3-5: his Knuckle Down (Q) engage and Haymaker (W) shield-punch win short trades, but by 6 your Q Darkin Glaive, E Golden Onslaught and Final Retribution let you match his all-in and start leveling the lane.
edits.after: Sett takes levels 2-3: Knuckle Down (Q) speed and Haymaker (W) win short trades, but Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 — step in the moment he spends it. By 6 The Darkin Glaive, Aureate Rush and Grim Deliverance match his all-in.

edits.before: With two items you clearly overtake him — bait his Haymaker (W), avoid his grit stored damage, and your sustained output grinds him down in every side-lane duel where his kit runs out of steam.
edits.after: With two items you clearly overtake him — bait Haymaker (W) before you commit, and skip stacking raw armour since its centre is true damage; your sustained output grinds him down in every side-lane duel.

notes: Best find: the page warned four separate times about 'his E stun', but Facebreaker only stuns when enemies sit on both sides of Sett — in a 1v1 lane it is a slow. Second: The Show Stopper grounds, which denies Aureate Rush, and that was never stated. Zaahen ability names come from the missing-interaction file and the mirror audit; his W and passive still have no verified name and are left unnamed.
